iconic_games_note: Lincoln Financial Field has a genuine international football history: it hosted three 2016 Copa America Centenario group matches (above, each verified) and the 2015 CONCACAF Gold Cup final (Mexico 3-1 Jamaica, July 26, 2015, att. 68,930), plus CONCACAF Gold Cup quarterfinal doubleheaders (2017, 2019), 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup matches, and USMNT/club friendlies. The authoritative dates for the three Copa America Centenario fixtures are June 9 (Uruguay-Venezuela), June 11 (USA-Paraguay) and June 14 (Chile-Panama), per Wikipedia/ESPN/SI/MLS/Philadelphia Union; the cited StadiumDB tournament page mis-lists them as June 10/12/15 (off by one), so the dates here follow the authoritative sources, not StadiumDB. Only the three fully-scored Copa America fixtures are shipped in iconic_games; the 2015 Gold Cup final and 2017/2019 quarterfinals are noted but not pinned to a single authoritative source in this pass.

city_history.significance: Philadelphia, founded by William Penn in 1682, was the largest city in the American colonies and served as the capital of the United States during much of the Revolutionary era. It is the birthplace of American independence: the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the U.S. Constitution (1787) were both signed at Independence Hall. The 2026 World Cup connection is symbolically charged, with Philadelphia hosting a Round of 16 match on July 4 — Independence Day — during the United States' 250th-anniversary year.
city_history.football_culture: Philadelphia is one of America's most passionate sports cities, with a famously fervent fan base across the Eagles (NFL), Phillies (MLB), 76ers (NBA) and Flyers (NHL). On the soccer side, the metro is home to MLS side Philadelphia Union (since 2010, at Subaru Park in Chester), and Lincoln Financial Field itself has hosted Copa America Centenario, the 2015 CONCACAF Gold Cup final, and USMNT matches, giving the city a real top-flight international football pedigree.

stadium_history_facts: Opened August 2003 (Wikipedia: August 3, 2003; StadiumDB: August 9, 2003), replacing Veterans Stadium as a purpose-built football venue.
Designed by NBBJ with Agoos Lovera Architects; structural engineering by Ove Arup & Partners.
Home of the Philadelphia Eagles (NFL) and Temple Owls (NCAA football) since 2003; also hosts soccer fixtures.
Located at 1020 Pattison Avenue, South Philadelphia, in the city's sports-complex district.
2013 renovation (~US$125 million) added ~11,000 solar panels and 14 wind turbines, generating roughly a third (30%) of the stadium's energy.
Hosted three 2016 Copa America Centenario group matches (June 9/11/14) and the 2015 CONCACAF Gold Cup final (Mexico 3-1 Jamaica, July 26, 2015).
For the 2026 World Cup it is renamed 'Philadelphia Stadium' and hosts six matches including a Round of 16 tie on July 4.
